headings.title: Introduction to Operating Room Environments
headings.content: An operating room, frequently called an operating theatre, is a specialized facility within a hospital where surgical operations are carried out in a sterile environment. The design and layout of these rooms prioritize patient safety, efficient workflow, and strict infection control. Environmental controls regulate temperature, humidity, and air pressure to minimize microbial contamination. Positive pressure ventilation ensures that when doors open, air flows outward rather than allowing unfiltered hallway air to enter. Zoned areas restrict access progressively, moving from unrestricted zones where street clothes are permitted to restricted zones where sterile attire and masks are mandatory.

headings.title: General Operating Theatres
headings.content: General operating theatres are versatile spaces equipped to handle a wide variety of routine and non-specialized surgical procedures. These rooms house standard surgical tables, basic electrocautery units, anesthesia machines, and standard instrument sets suitable for procedures like appendectomies, hernia repairs, and basic exploratory laparotomies. Because they accommodate multiple surgical specialties, their equipment must be mobile and easily reconfigured between cases.

headings.title: Specialized Operating Theatres
headings.content:
Specialized operating theatres are dedicated environments tailored for specific surgical disciplines that require unique, fixed technology. Unlike versatile general rooms, these suites contain integrated equipment that cannot be easily moved.

- **Cardiothoracic Theatre**: Features heart-lung bypass machine hookups, specialized perfusion monitors, and advanced imaging integration.
- **Neurosurgical Theatre**: Equipped with stereotactic frame systems, operating microscopes, and high-precision neurological navigation tools.
- **Orthopedic Theatre**: Houses heavy traction equipment, orthopedic power tools, and specialized radiolucent imaging tables.
- **Ophthalmic Theatre**: Designed with micro-surgical microscopes and compact instrumentation suited for delicate eye tissues.

headings.title: Modular Theatres
headings.content: Modular theatres are constructed using pre-fabricated, high-grade antimicrobial wall panels made of stainless steel or specialized laminates. These panels eliminate joints and crevices where dust and bacteria accumulate. Services such as medical gases, electrical outlets, and digital integration screens are flush-mounted. This design allows for rapid assembly, easy maintenance, and future technological upgrades without extensive structural demolition.

headings.title: Emergency and Trauma Operating Suites
headings.content: Trauma operating suites are positioned close to emergency departments to manage life-threatening injuries requiring immediate surgical intervention. Speed is critical in these environments. Consequently, these rooms maintain constant readiness with pre-staged massive transfusion protocols, rapid infusion devices, and comprehensive trauma carts. The surgical team must be capable of initiating damage control surgery—focusing on hemorrhage control and contamination containment rather than definitive anatomical repair.

headings.title: Infection Control and Zoning in Operating Rooms
headings.content:
Maintaining sterility within the surgical suite relies on strict spatial zoning and rigorous protocols. The facility is divided into four distinct zones:

- **Unrestricted Zone**: Street clothes are permitted; administrative tasks and patient reception occur here.
- **Semi-Restricted Zone**: Scrub suits and hair covers are mandatory; this includes corridors, instrument processing areas, and recovery spaces.
- **Restricted Zone**: Masks, eye protection, and full surgical attire are required; this encompasses the actual operating theatre and sterile core.
- **Sterile Field**: The immediate area surrounding the draped patient and sterile instrument tables, touched only by personnel in sterile gowns and gloves.
